source_notes.finding: @ai-sdk/code-mode depends only on `run` (package.json dependencies: run ^2.1.8). runCodeMode builds a Run runner with createRunner, wraps the user's source, exposes every AI SDK tool as one Run host group `__codeMode` (tool0, tool1, ..., missing), and returns result.value. Limits, continuations and approvals are Run features re-exported under code-mode names.

The guest sees a `tools` Proxy; property access maps a tool name to its __codeMode.toolN binding or to __codeMode.missing. The model sees a TypeScript `declare const tools: {...}` block plus example calls generated from each tool's JSON Schema (input and output types, descriptions as JSDoc).
source_notes.evidence: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L209-L217 and tool-prompt.ts#L15-L47; generated text saved in research/probes/vercel-ai-sdk-codemode/out/P1.json (toolDescriptionSeenByModel)

source_notes.finding: Default toolDiscovery 'description' puts every tool's signature in the code_mode tool description. toolDiscovery 'conversation' keeps the description fixed and sends a catalog as a user message; combined with the AI SDK's toolSearch() and deferLoading tools, only discovered tools enter the catalog, so it can scale past 100 tools.

Run's async host-function bridge (worker postMessage to the main thread); each tool call runs invokeHostTool on the host, which validates input with the tool's schema (only if the schema has a validator), checks needsApproval, and calls the tool's execute with the outer abort signal.

Same as vercel-run: QuickJS WASM in a worker thread, fresh context, Function and eval blocked. The docs call the sandbox "defense in depth" and say tools run on the host with full authority; the code matches.
runCodeMode returns only the JSON round-tripped return value. Nothing in packages/code-mode/src captures console output (grep finds no console handling outside tests), so the model never sees logs.

Run errors are translated to CodeMode* error classes (timeout, CPU timeout, bridge limit, source too large); the stack is rewritten from run.js to code-mode.js with the wrapper line removed. Any non-CodeModeError thrown by a tool becomes "Host tool failed."

Approval: callback mode or interrupt mode with HMAC-signed continuations (default signing key is random per process). The docs say code mode does not integrate with AI SDK approval flows and nested tools needing approval are rejected, while the code ships an interrupt-based approval path. Apache-2.0, part of vercel/ai, last commit 2026-11-20.

surprises: The docs list console.log, console.info, console.debug and console.error as supported in programs (18-code-mode.mdx:196), and the tool's own guidance never says logs are invisible, but console output goes to the server's stdout and never into the tool result. A model that debugs with console.log sees nothing.

The docs say code mode "does not currently integrate with AI SDK tool approval flows" and nested approval tools are rejected, yet the package exports an interrupt-based approval API (experimental_continueCodeModeApproval, approval.mode 'interrupt').
Input validation depends on the tool's schema object: a jsonSchema() without a validate function passed {id: "not-a-number"} straight to execute (P10d). With zod schemas it validates.
Going over 32 concurrent tool calls fails the whole execution after the first 32 calls already ran, which can leave side effects behind.
